meaning:
θροέω, -ῶ
(θρόος, a noise, tumult), [in LXX: Sng.5:4 (הָמָה * ;]
in cl.,
1. to cry aloud, make an outcry.
2. to utter aloud.
3. In NT (and LXX), pass., to be troubled, as by an alarm: Mat.24:6, Mrk.13:7, Luk.24:37 (WH, mg.), 2Th.2:2 (cf. Kennedy, Sources, 126).†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: You will hear of wars and rumors of wars. See that you aren’t troubled, for all this must happen, but the end is not yet.
“When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, don’t be troubled. For those must happen, but the end is not yet.
not to be quickly shaken in your mind, and not be troubled, either by spirit, or by word, or by letter as if from us, saying that the day of Christ has already…
